items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: and Chubby Jackson was on the band.

ctx.x: When I was with Barnett? Let me see. Al Killiqn was on the band, on trumpet, and Dick Vance was on the band on trumpet, myself, and Chubby Jackson was on the band. This is before he went with Woody Herman. And Ralph Burns was on the band, later went with Woody Herman.

Buddy DeFranco was on the band, clarinet man, and -- see who else I can remember. Don Lamond was on the band, drummer. Lot of people knew Don. And those are about the guys I remember from the band, but he had some good players on the band.

items.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: And word was passed through to Trummy to get off the bandstand very quietly. And I had one of those big, black plastic bass cases. And it fit him.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about a couple of little things that I read and I often wondered if they could possibly be true. Something about Trummy Young hiding in your bass case?

Oh yeah. That was with Charlie Barnet’s band. This is true. We were playing, and backstage, we’re on stage, and backstage there are two guys with a vest, and they really looked like who they were. They were C-O-P-S. And Charlie went off the stage while the band was doing something, and he’s talking to them. Of course he was probably afraid somebody in the band was in trouble of some sort you know. And that’s beside the point. But at any rate, the next tune was “Mood Indigo.” And on account of that, all the lights…
